chunks: Say: 'Whose is the sovereignty over all things, who protects, and against whom there is no protection? {Answer} if you have knowledge.'

key_terms.تَعْلَمُونَ: You know (implying those with true knowledge acknowledge this)
key_terms.مَلَكُوتُ: Sovereignty or dominion, referring to the inner, spiritual, and absolute kingdom of God
key_terms.وَلَا يُجَارُ عَلَيْهِ: And against whom there is no protection (He is secure from others)

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'Malakut' signify in the Quran regarding God's sovereignty?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to affirm God's absolute dominion (Malakut) and self-sufficiency (Al-Ghani), contrasting His eternal security with the contingent nature of creation. It underscores that while all authority and protection are derived from Him, He remains independent of any external aid, a concept central to understanding divine unity (Tawhid) and the hierarchy of being.
